They fed on fruit and other vegetation that would ferment in their pot-bellies. Colourful primate often made for exotic pets; these sociable animals were spread to multiple worlds, where escaped wild populations soon established themselves. Visible features it must show: the canon Yavin 4 woolamander (see canon entry woolamander): ONE animal, alone, with no branch, perch or hanging ornament; a colourful furred primate; a round pot-belly; an exceptionally long bare tail. Keep the colourful furred primate body, the round pot-belly, the bare face and bare hands, and the palette exactly as in the previous render. Fur: painted as soft, irregular masses of colour with gentle tonal variation and natural light from above; individual hairs blend into the mass rather than appearing as separate drawn lines. The bare face and hands are smooth, modelled skin with natural painted light and shadow. Edges: soft and painted, a subtle slightly deeper shade of the local colour, just enough for readability. Tail, in every facing: a bare, hairless, slender cord tail leaves the base of the spine and trails down and back along the ground behind the animal. The cord is clearly longer than the arms, more than twice the length from shoulder to fingertip, and it is the longest single line of the animal. It runs well past the feet and ends in a rainbow-striped fur bulb that rests on the ground far behind and below the feet line, clearly separated from the body. In the rear view and the side view the full length of the cord is visible as a long, sweeping line from rump to bulb. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body and the whole tail visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.
